research_question: Does synchronized Camera B depth supervision materially improve single Camera A RGB+K feed-forward MHR over equal-budget single-view surface supervision?

why.detail: M wins seed 20260910 but loses seed 20260911; its 0.615 mm paired-seed mean advantage is below the preregistered 2 mm threshold.

nonsealed_conclusions: Pose/camera-only surface finetuning materially improves absolute V2 VAL error over Official, TRAIN-only Txyz, and Historical V1 E1 at the selected checkpoint.
Aligned error improves over Official/Txyz but is not better than Historical V1 E1, so superior non-translation geometry over the strongest historical comparator is not established.
Synchronized two-view depth supervision has no material benefit under the equal-budget two-seed protocol.
The credible LBS-derived torso map is coarse and cannot identify back surface or acupuncture regions.

next_experiment.only_recommendation: keep arm S and add a protective/non-regression gate or loss against Official on already-low-error samples
next_experiment.reason: On one-shot V2 SEALED, only 6/12 subjects improve versus Official and all five Official-below-30-mm subjects regress. Shape/Scale, synthetic, LoRA, and more data do not directly test this observed failure first.

claim_boundary: The result supports lower mean and tail error on HuMMan dataset-ROI SEALED subjects, but not robust per-subject improvement, automatic raw-image operation, back-surface accuracy, acupuncture localization, or deployment.
